pr_title: Feature: allow to unwatch a repo
pr_body:
<!--
  Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!
  To reference an open issue, please write this in your description: `Fixes #NUMBER`
-->
Fixes #8139 

This PR adds a new command `subscription` for managing subscriptions of watched repos. This is a WIP, but I would like to ensure that this is on the right track.

### Current Progress
Added `gh subscription list` command following `project-layout.md` guidelines. Since the REST API returns a list of repositories, I choose to use the same output format as `gh repo list`. Flag `-L, --limit` is included to limit the maximum number of listed repositories.

Tests are not written yet. I aim to execute tests similar to those for existing `list` subcommands. However, I'm not quite sure about the usage among `fixture/` and various types of responses in `httpmock` for these stub tests. Please advise if I've misunderstood the nuances of stub test implementation.

### Upcoming Tasks
Plan to implement:
`subscription get OWNER/REPO` Displays subscription status (all/ignored/unwatched).
`subscription set OWNER/REPO <all/ignore>` Sets subscription status.
`subscription unwatch OWNER/REPO` Deletes repository subscription.*
*Not sure if unwatch should be implemented as a subcommand(`unwatch` or `delete`) or an option in `set` subcommand as its not mentioned in the issue.

Seeking suggestions to ensure reliable implementation.
Review and insights are greatly appreciated!
pr_comments:
Hi @andyfeller ,
Thanks for the reviews and suggestions! I will try to make the language used more aligned with existing commands.

This PR is now ready for review.

The new command `gh subscription` (alias `gh sub`) is added, with the following subcommands:
- `gh subscription list`: List repositories watched by the authenticated user
- `gh subscription view`: Display whether subscribed to a GitHub repository for notifications
- `gh subscription edit`: Edit subscription settings (currently only `--notify` for toggle all notifications)
- `gh subscription delete`: Delete subscription to a repository (unwatch the repository)

If there are any adjustments needed, please let me know, thank you!

issue_context.title: Feature: allow users to subscribe to various subscribable objects
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I am often added to repositories in my organization. I'd like to manually unwatch those I don't need.

### Proposed solution

I would like, via the CLI, to know the current "watching" setting for a repo, and change it.
comments:
@GuillaumeDesforges : thank you for opening up this suggestion! 🤗 

**What might some of the commands to view, subscribe, and unsubscribe from watched repositories look like?**

- Which top level command would this be under?
  - `gh repo`
  - `gh watch`
  - `gh repo-watch`
- How impactful would it be if no additional filters could be applied?
  - not which org
  - not with any repo topics
  - etc

For information on the REST APIs for watching repositories, see [Activity > Watching](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/activity/watching?apiVersion=2022-11-28).

Thanks for the questions @andyfeller 

Given that the REST API is about "subscription" I could see

```
# add a filter to gh repo list

gh repo list --subscription all
gh repo list --subscription participating+mention
gh repo list --subscription ignore

# add a subscription command

# get subscription for a specific repo
gh subscription get cli/cli
# set subscription for a specific repo
gh subscription set cli/cli all
gh subscription set cli/cli ignore
```

I'm not so sold on any shape, but rather the ability to know/set subscription on a repo.

> ```
> # add a filter to gh repo list
> 
> gh repo list --subscription all
> gh repo list --subscription participating+mention
> gh repo list --subscription ignore
> ```

My hesitance with adding a `--subscription` flag to `gh repo list` is all of the other flags wouldn't be applicable when looking for subscriptions.  Even these flag values don't appear within the GitHub APIs; all you get are the repositories the authenticated user is subscribed to / watching.

My opinion is that this might simply be `gh subscription list` with a possible alias of `sub` to shorten the command.

> `gh subscription list` with a possible alias of `sub` to shorten the command

That makes sense :+1:

Hi @andyfeller 
I am currently trying to work on this and the progress is stated in the PR. I'm not sure whether any adjustments might be needed, or if I can proceed with working on this feature?

@nelsonchen304 : thank you for your patience!  yes, this issue is up for grabs being marked `help wanted` and I see the draft PR you were alluding to.  I'm going to look at the draft now and can leave any commentary to help continue your momentum 🙇 🤗

Following up on https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/8393#issuecomment-1883306446, there has been some considerable discussion with other core maintainers regarding how to proceed overall with the crux of discussion revolving around:

1. the ability to subscribe to various objects _(organization, user, repository, issue, pull request, discussion)_
2. the added complexity and supportability of the feature for the team

## Understanding how the proposed feature supports other types of subscriptions

**One of the biggest concerns raised by fellow maintainers is accommodating other types of subscription.**

Beyond the REST endpoints for working with repository subscriptions / watches, the GraphQL API provides [`updateSubscription`](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#updatesubscription) and [unsubscribeFromNotifications](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#unsubscribefromnotifications) mutations for working with a broader variety of [`Subscribable` objects](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/interfaces#subscribable) including:

- issues
- discussions
- commits
- repositories
- pull requests
- team discussions
- teams

with users and organizations being managed by [followOrganization](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#followorganization) and [followUser](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/mutations#followuser).

Planning for supporting these other objects would change the nature of the commands used as they would likely follow the form of:

- `gh <object> ignore <graphql id>`
- `gh <object> subscribe <graphql id>`
- `gh <object> unsubscribe <graphql id>`

### Considerations

Using the `Subscribable` approach, we would need to change logic to leverage `viewerCanSubscribe` and `viewerSubscription` fields to determine if users can change the subscription state and what it is.  The biggest question is whether there is a way to list and search for types of objects that the user is subscribed to 🤔 

## Addressing added complexity and supportability

Between adding a whole class of command and subcommands which @nelsonchen304 has already graciously put the effort forth 🙇 , I wonder if refactoring this based on the new subcommands mentioned above makes it more palatable. 🤔

That makes good sense, thanks for sharing!
In that framing, how would one typically list the ID of subscribed objects?
E.g., how can I list the ID of subscribed repos?
Additionally, how would that work for repo subscription "all" vs "participating & mentions"?
Thanks!

@GuillaumeDesforges : I haven't had luck figuring out an ideal, efficient way to search for / list subscribable objects yet. 🤷 

There are no [search qualifiers for issue or PR subscriptions](https://docs.github.com/en/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-issues-and-pull-requests) much less the other objects.  I think repositories might be the only object you can get that information from.  Otherwise, you have to pull everything back and filter it client side based on `viewerSubscription` details.

### Where do we go from here?

This issue in the UI:

![Image](https://github.com/cli/cli/assets/2089743/9a0bf868-076b-46c7-8604-04355be4809c)

This issue in the CLI:

```shell

  ### Proposed solution                                                                                               
                                                                                                                      
  I would like, via the CLI, to know the current "watching" setting for a repo, and change it.                        


———————— Not showing 8 comments ————————


GuillaumeDesforges • Jan  9, 2024 • Newest comment
1 👀

  That makes good sense, thanks for sharing!                                                                          
  In that framing, how would one typically list the ID of subscribed objects?                                         
  E.g., how can I list the ID of subscribed repos?                                                                    
  Additionally, how would that work for repo subscription "all" vs "participating & mentions"?                        
  Thanks!                                                                                                             


Use --comments to view the full conversation
View this issue on GitHub: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8139
```

My current thoughts are:

1. We could add `ignore` / `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` subcommands to all of the subscribable objects we  support in the GitHub CLI
2. We could add `list-subscriptions` to `gh repo` as that appears to be the only object the APIs will provide this info
3. We could enhance the `view` subcommands for the different subscribable objects to include viewer's subscription information
4. We could enhance the `--json` fields for the different subscribable objects include the viewer's subscription
5. In the far future if we can get support for listing other types of subscriptions, we can add `list-subscriptions` to those when possible 🤷 

@GuillaumeDesforges @nelsonchen304 @williammartin  : what do you think?
Sounds like it would help me do what I need, thanks :+1:

> This could potentially be used to implement `list-subscriptions` for `gh issue`. Unfortunately, I haven’t found a similar filter for other objects, so this approach may not be universally applicable.

Yeah, sadly this is a gap on the GitHub side as issues and PRs are managed by different teams.  Normally both areas would have parity as issues and PRs are closely related. 🤷

This might simply be where only some primitives can offer this experience:

1. issues
2. repositories

> As for the `ignore`, `subscribe`, and `unsubscribe` subcommands, I’m wondering if we should adopt a consistent format like `gh <object> ignore/subscribe/unsubscribe <graphql id>`, as mentioned above:

Agreed.

> From a user perspective, gh issue unsubscribe <issue number> seems more intuitive and aligns with existing commands like gh issue view <issue number>. While querying an ID from an issue/pr number is straightforward, I haven’t explored other subscribable objects in detail, so I’m unsure if this approach would be effective across the board. 🤔

Agreed.  Most commands allow users to provide a URL or a number, which is resolved to appropriate graphQL IDs as needed behind the scenes.

> I’d greatly appreciate your insights or thoughts on this.

I think we have enough perspective on how this would fit into `gh` from a command perspective and we understand where certain limitations are.

The body of work here is significantly large, so it would be best to figure out where to start and creating separate issues for different command sets.

**Is there anything else I'm missing?**

Yes, I think we’ve gained a good overview. Nothing else comes to mind at the moment.

Here are some of my initial thoughts:

Maybe we should start by adding these subcommands(`ignore`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, `list-subscription`) and enhancing current ones (`view`, `--json`) for `gh repo` since it is well-supported by the APIs and solves the original issue.

As for other commands, at least `list-subscription` should be separated for those without API support.

Additionally, would it be better to break down the adding command part and enhancing part to separate issues?
